verses.text: This is the message of judgment against Damascus: "Look, Damascus will no longer be a city. It will become a heap of ruins.
The cities of Aroer will be deserted. They will become places for flocks to lie down, and no one will scare them away.
The strong cities of Ephraim will disappear, and the kingdom of Damascus will come to an end. The survivors of Syria will be like the faded glory of the people of Israel," says the LORD of Armies.
"On that day the glory of Jacob will fade, and his strong body will waste away.
It will be like a harvester gathering wheat, cutting the grain with his arm. It will be like someone picking up the leftover grain in the Valley of Rephaim.

Yet some will be left, like the olives left after an olive tree is beaten, two or three at the very top of the tree, four or five on the outer branches of a fruit tree," says the LORD, the God of Israel.
On that day people will look to their Maker, and their eyes will turn to the Holy One of Israel.
They will no longer look to the altars they made with their own hands. They will not respect what their fingers have made, the Asherah poles or the incense altars.
On that day their strong cities will be like deserted places in the forests and on the hilltops, which people left when the Israelites came. Everything will be ruined.
For you have forgotten the God who saves you. You have not remembered the Rock who makes you strong. So you plant beautiful gardens and set out vines from foreign lands.
On the day you plant them, you put a fence around them. In the morning you make your seeds sprout. But the harvest will disappear on a day of sickness and pain that cannot be cured.
Oh, the roaring of many peoples, roaring like the roaring of the seas! The rushing of nations, rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!

The nations rush like the rushing of mighty waters, but when God speaks sternly to them, they run far away. They are chased away like chaff blown by the wind on the hills, like dust whirling in a storm.
In the evening, look, there is sudden terror! By morning they are gone. This is what happens to those who rob us. This is the fate of those who steal from us.
